workshop_summary:
Objective: sizing workshop to recommend reserved GPU footprint, burst policy, and SLA terms.

Observed baseline traffic: steady-state 45-60 qps (chat/support) + 25 qps embeddings batch jobs during off-peak.
Peak events: market open spikes up to 520 qps for short-generation (primarily 8-40 token responses) for ~3-7 minute windows; secondary spikes from downstream reranking jobs.
Token characteristics: avg response tokens 22 for chat flows; embeddings jobs produce 768-d vectors but are batched (avg batch size 64).
Desired SLOs: 95th percentile latency < 120ms for short-chat responses (<=64 tokens), 99th percentile < 350ms; steady-state throughput guarantee 600 qps combined with 2x burst capacity for 10 minute windows.
Capacity recommendation: start with 8x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs reserved for steady-state (estimated sustained throughput ~300 qps for generation workloads with continuous batching and KV cache), plus 4x burst GPUs available via autoscale/burst pool for peak windows. Provides headroom and aligns with cost target.
Throughput guarantees & SLA asks: guaranteed baseline qps of 300 with documented linear degradation policy and prioritized routing; incident SLA 1-hour for failover to secondary region; financial credits tiered by percentage of downtime or SLO misses.
Autoscaling & routing: prefer policy-based routing — critical trading inference pinned to dedicated pool, non-critical embeddings shifted to lower-cost private pool; automatic fallback to a smaller model variant when tailing capacity.
Operational items: enable prefix/KV caching for session-based trading prompts, token-level cost reporting, per-route latency dashboards, rollout canaries.
Open technical questions: expected KV cache hit-rate assumptions (customer to provide telemetry), exact token distribution by endpoint, regulatory constraint on cross-region failover.
Recommended next steps: confirm expected TTL and cache hit-rate, run one-day stress test with synthetic spikes (simulate 10x for 5 minutes), draft SLA language and GPU SKU options for procurement.
